Only one quality session (tempo on Friday) maintains lactate-threshold stimulus without double-hard-day fatigue. Rest days dominate. Athlete should feel fresher by end of Week 4 and ready for the next build block. HRV should trend upward; RHR should normalize. Paces: Easy 6:40–6:50/km, Tempo 5:52/km.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes a polarized aerobic foundation (80/20 easy-to-hard ratio) scaled to your current Strava fitness (Easy 6:40/km, Tempo 5:52/km). Week 1 starts conservatively at ~42 km, building from your recent 26 km / 14-day average. Weeks 2–3 progress volume progressively (+8% → +5%) to reach a peak of 48 km and a 14 km long run, introducing two quality sessions per week (tempo + intervals/fartlek) spaced safely away from the long run. Week 4 is a planned recovery week (−20% volume, reduced long run to 11.2 km, one quality session only) to consolidate adaptations. All workouts are color-coded by intensity (Easy Zone 1–2, Hard Zone 3–4) and include exact paces from your Strava profile. Use this block to build aerobic base, practice fueling/hydration in long runs, and prepare for the next Aerobic Development block (Weeks 5–8), which will introduce marathon-pace segments and longer sustained tempo efforts. No race date is set, so phases are labeled by position in the 16-week cycle; adjust the schedule when a race date is confirmed.
